key_insight: CONES is extended from fixed losses to time-varying convex losses, showing that one can still trade off regret and movement while staying feasible in a nested evolving constraint set.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for real-time decision systems with changing objectives and constraints, where the optimizer must adapt smoothly without large action jumps.
method: Projected proximal algorithm for online optimization over nested feasible sets
Achieves simultaneous regret-movement tradeoffs for convex losses: O(T^{1-β}) regret and O(T^β) movement
Strongly convex losses yield O(1) regret with O(log T) movement
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret and movement bounds, plus lower bounds showing these tradeoffs are near-unavoidable for weakly adaptive and anytime online algorithms.
watch_item: The guarantees are asymptotic and theoretical, so practical performance may depend on how expensive projection/proximal steps are and how well the nested feasible sets are modeled.
paper_title: Convex Optimization with Nested Evolving Feasible Sets (CONES) under Time-Varying Loss Functions
